full.description: This is a low-power photomicrograph of a cross-section of the colon stained with H&E. The section shows colonic mucosa with crypts, submucosa, and muscularis propria layers. Prominent lymphoid aggregates are visible in the mucosa and submucosa, suggestive of chronic inflammation. The overall architecture is characteristic of colonic tissue involved in inflammatory conditions or architectural alterations.

The abnormality is consistent with a meningomyelocele, involving the meninges and spinal cord. The tissue shows classic structural displacement associated with this congenital condition.

random.description: This image is a photomicrograph of a cross-section of the appendix, likely showing the lumen and surrounding wall layers. The mucosa displays chronic inflammation with lymphoid follicles, while the deeper muscularis layers show fibrosis and scarring. These histological features are characteristic of chronic appendicitis. The H&E stain highlights the architectural changes and inflammatory cell infiltration within the appendiceal wall.
